Publication-ready tables

Source: R/tables.R
irt_table.Rd

Turns IRTistic results into clean, consistently formatted tables: numbers rounded to a fixed number of decimals, p-values in APA style ("< .001"), estimates optionally combined with their standard errors as "1.23 (0.05)", and a caption and note attached. Tables can be returned as a data frame or rendered as Markdown, HTML or LaTeX (via 'knitr'), and written to `.csv`, `.html`, `.md` or `.tex` files.

Usage

irt_table(
  x,
  digits = 2,
  format = c("data.frame", "markdown", "html", "latex"),
  file = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object to tabulate.

digits

Number of decimals.

format

`"data.frame"` (default), `"markdown"`, `"html"` or `"latex"`.

file

Optional output file; the format is taken from the extension (`.csv`, `.html`, `.md`, `.tex`).

caption

Table caption (a sensible default is used).

...

Further arguments for specific methods: `se` (combine estimates and SEs, default `TRUE`) for `irtfit`; `facet` for facet reports.

Value

An `irt_table` (a data frame with `caption` and `note` attributes), or a 'knitr' table for the other formats. Written files are returned invisibly.

Details

Supported inputs: `irtfit` (item parameters), `mfrmfit` / `mfrm_report` (facet measurement reports), and the outputs of [item_fit()], [person_fit()], [sx2()], [reliability()], [dif_test()], [dif_irt()], [mfrm_bias()], [classification_accuracy()], [cat_simulate()], [score_table()], [equate_true_score()], as well as any data frame.

Examples

fit <- irt_fit(sim_irt(500, 8, "2pl"), "2pl")
irt_table(fit)
#> Item parameter estimates
#> 
#>  Item Model           a            b
#>   I01   2pl 1.26 (0.28)  2.39 (0.38)
#>   I02   2pl 1.34 (0.22)  0.57 (0.11)
#>   I03   2pl 1.55 (0.26)  0.37 (0.09)
#>   I04   2pl 1.16 (0.19)  0.21 (0.10)
#>   I05   2pl 0.51 (0.14)  1.41 (0.39)
#>   I06   2pl 1.14 (0.20) -0.23 (0.10)
#>   I07   2pl 0.80 (0.15) -0.07 (0.13)
#>   I08   2pl 0.79 (0.16) -0.48 (0.15)
#> 
#> Note. Marginal maximum likelihood estimates; standard errors in parentheses. a =
#>       discrimination, b = difficulty / threshold, g = lower asymptote, u = upper
#>       asymptote. N = 500, log-likelihood = -2373.83, AIC = 4779.7, BIC = 4847.1.
irt_table(item_fit(fit), format = "markdown")
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Item fit statistics
#> 
#> |Item | Measure|   SE|   N| Infit MNSQ| Infit ZSTD| Outfit MNSQ| Outfit ZSTD| Obs. avg| Exp. avg| Pt-measure r|       Flag|
#> |:----|-------:|----:|---:|----------:|----------:|-----------:|-----------:|--------:|--------:|------------:|----------:|
#> |I01  |    2.39| 0.38| 462|       1.01|       0.14|        0.80|       -0.90|     0.08|     0.07|         0.36| productive|
#> |I02  |    0.57| 0.11| 462|       0.83|      -4.01|        0.78|       -3.98|     0.38|     0.36|         0.60| productive|
#> |I03  |    0.37| 0.09| 462|       0.77|      -5.41|        0.69|       -5.67|     0.42|     0.41|         0.66| productive|
#> |I04  |    0.21| 0.10| 462|       0.86|      -4.22|        0.83|       -4.52|     0.48|     0.47|         0.54| productive|
#> |I05  |    1.41| 0.39| 462|       1.01|       0.19|        1.00|        0.14|     0.36|     0.34|         0.21| productive|
#> |I06  |   -0.23| 0.10| 462|       0.86|      -4.31|        0.82|       -4.28|     0.59|     0.58|         0.51| productive|
#> |I07  |   -0.07| 0.13| 462|       0.94|      -2.53|        0.93|       -2.61|     0.55|     0.53|         0.37| productive|
#> |I08  |   -0.48| 0.15| 462|       0.94|      -2.19|        0.92|       -2.26|     0.62|     0.60|         0.34| productive|
#> 
#> *Note.* MNSQ = mean-square; ZSTD = Wilson-Hilferty standardised mean-square. Productive range 0.5-1.5.
